answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can influence a decision, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. The stake is tied to the action, not merely to an account, so creating a thousand identities does not multiply cheap influence: each one must lock real value and risk losing it. A basalt ledger can record deposits and penalties, while zenith and nectar serve as harmless agent names; the attacker pays in capital, opportunity cost, and exposure to repeated audits.
